about: What a hair salon may change in the Ochre & Ash design. Protected: the scroll-run appointment (one head of hair, strand by strand: consultation, sectioning, hand-painting, processing, toning, the cut and the blow-out), the shade finder's strands and its lift rules, the menu with stylist levels, the hair portraits of the team, the booking flow, layout, type and all interaction code. The salon's own words, services and prices, levels, team, hours, the example client's colour and the shade looks come from the content.
rules: Text may not contain < > { } or line breaks.

stages: the seven steps of the colour appointment the hero shows, in order: consultation, sectioning, painting, processing, toning, the cut, blow-out. Each has a short name, a caption in the salon's voice and a clock time.

client: the example client's natural level (1 black to 10 lightest blonde), the level the painted pieces lift to, the toner (a short name and its colour), minutes processing and centimetres trimmed. The captions must match these numbers.
menu: one to three stylist levels (tiers) and one to three groups of services; each service has an id (lowercase), a name, a line, minutes and one price per level, in the order of the levels.

shade.looks: two to six looks the shade finder offers, each with how many levels it lifts (negative goes darker), the service it books (svc, a menu id), how it is placed (all over, fine lights, or ribbons) and a title.
team.people: two to four colourists, each with their level (lv, the index into menu.tiers), what they are known for, their own hair colour (base and lift, levels 1-10) and when they are next free.
book: the deposit, the service the booking starts on (first, a menu id), the label for any colourist, the opening hours for each day (null when closed) and the policy line.
